blocks.text: Aldergrove Mobile Homes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Aldergrove is a community in the Township of Langley: the Township states its eastern boundary is 276 Street, bordering the City of Abbotsford, and its southern boundary is the United States border — Aldergrove's one manufactured-home community sits on that southern boundary.

blocks.text: Aldergrove Mobile Homes: the housing stock

items.t: The buyer owns the manufactured home and holds co-operative shares and occupancy rights — the land is held through the co-operative, so this is neither fee-simple land ownership, nor a strata lot, nor a Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act (MHPTA) pad tenancy.
Verified pad-rental parks in Aldergrove: none.

Not Aldergrove stock, by name: Creekside Villa, 27435 29A Avenue, is a gated 55+ rancher townhouse strata, and Alderwood Manor, 27090 32 Avenue, is built townhouse form — neither is a manufactured-home park, and Langley Grove Estates is Otter District ground, not Aldergrove.
That line describes Brookswood's parks; at Pioneer Park there is no pad and no landlord, and the co-operative's share and occupancy documents replace the pad tenancy entirely.

blocks.text: Aldergrove Mobile Homes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A Pioneer Park purchase has two records to diligence, not one: the provincial Manufactured Home Registry record for the home itself, and the co-operative's share and occupancy record — the Registry transfer alone does not transfer co-op membership or acceptance.

Township frame for Aldergrove ground: Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw 1987 No. 2500 and the Aldergrove Community Plan govern the land under and around Pioneer Park, and the Township's small-scale multi-unit housing Bylaw No.

blocks.text: Aldergrove Mobile Homes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Pioneer Park runs on a third legal system: not strata (no Form B, no strata bylaws) and not a pad tenancy (no pad-rent cap, no Residential Tenancy Branch pad process) — its acceptance, share and occupancy documents are the whole rulebook, and diligence done in either of the other two forms asks the wrong questions.

Pioneer Park's address is the border: 27111 0 Avenue is Aldergrove's south edge on the United States boundary, a rural setting apart from the Fraser Highway core — the opposite corner of the community from the Aldergrove Credit Union Community Centre at 27032 Fraser Highway.

Bertrand Creek bounds the Aldergrove Core Area to the north and east, so core-adjacent lots — not the 0 Avenue park site — are the ones where a watercourse and riparian check matters most; the Township directs applicants to check watercourses in its GeoSource mapping before applying.

Schools physically in Aldergrove, School District No. 35: Parkside Centennial Elementary (3300 270 Street), Shortreed Community Elementary (27330 28 Avenue), Coghlan Fundamental Elementary (4452 256 Street), North Otter Elementary (5370 248 Street), Betty Gilbert Middle School (26845 27 Avenue) and Aldergrove Community Secondary (26850 29 Avenue) — catchments are by address on the district locator, never by community name.

The nearest hospital confirmed on a health-authority source is Langley Memorial Hospital, 22051 Fraser Highway, west of Aldergrove in Murrayville; no urgent care centre or public health unit inside Aldergrove itself was verified.

Much of the Township's land is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and Aldergrove's rural fringe is where that bites: a manufactured home on an owned rural lot near Aldergrove can face reserve housing rules that a park home never meets.

items.t: Soil deposit applications in the Aldergrove area, Township of Langley: the Township's engagement page lists Aldergrove-area soil deposit applications for public feedback — STATUS: listed as an engagement item when read on 2026-11-03; soil movement on rural Aldergrove lots is the live application type touching the community's fringe, not a park application.

Aldergrove Community Plan update materials, Township of Langley: the redlined Aldergrove Community Plan sets the core bounded by Bertrand Creek, 29 Avenue and 270 Street — STATUS: plan document current when read on 2026-11-03; Pioneer Park at 27111 0 Avenue sits outside that core, under the plan's rural and border-edge policies.

blocks.text: Aldergrove Mobile Homes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Manufactured Home Registry check: the home at Pioneer Park still needs its provincial Registry record — a sale or transfer is effective only if registered, filed through a lawyer or notary with the original signed Bill of Sale and Notice to Transfer or Change Ownership — and the Registry record says nothing about co-op acceptance or shares.

Land check: confirm Pioneer Park's zoning under Township Zoning Bylaw 1987 No. 2500 and search the Township development applications page for 27111 0 Avenue — zoning confirms the land's designated use, not the co-operative's internal financial or occupancy position.

faq.q: Is Pioneer Park a pad-rental park like the Brookswood parks?
faq.a: No, and the difference changes the whole purchase. At Cedar Creek Estates or Fernridge Park you own the home and rent a pad from a landlord under provincial tenancy law. At Pioneer Park, 27111 0 Avenue, you own the home, buy co-operative shares, pay a monthly co-op charge, and must be accepted by the co-operative — there is no landlord, no pad rent and no tenancy agreement.

faq.q: Does the provincial pad-rent cap protect my monthly charge at Pioneer Park?
faq.a: No. The cap — one increase a year on 3 full months' notice, 2026 at 2.3% plus a proportional amount — applies to manufactured home site tenancies. A co-operative charge is set under the co-operative's own documents and bylaws, not the tenancy cap, so ask the co-operative how its charge is set and how it has changed, in writing, before an offer.

faq.q: What happens if Pioneer Park ever winds up or closes?
faq.a: Not the provincial park-closure route. Read the co-op documents, not the tenancy pages, for this question.

faq.q: Can I just move a manufactured home onto a rural Aldergrove lot instead?
faq.a: That is a land question, not a park question. Rural Aldergrove lots sit under Township zoning and, for many parcels, Agricultural Land Reserve rules — the Agricultural Land Commission's housing-in-the-ALR pages govern what housing the reserve allows, and the home itself still needs its Manufactured Home Registry record and CSA (Canadian Standards Association) label to be sold or moved.
